articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Málaga vs Villarreal
articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Málaga y Villarreal en La Rosaleda correspondiente a la jornada 6 de LaLiga EA Sports 26-27
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Málaga y Villarreal en La Rosaleda correspondiente a la jornada 6 de LaLiga EA Sports 26-27
articles.body: El Málaga afronta su regreso a Primera División con el objetivo de conseguir por fin su primera victoria del curso. El conjunto andaluz, eso sí, viene de sacar un valioso empate ante el Celta en Balaídos. La Rosaleda se presenta ahora como el escenario perfecto para buscar ese primer triunfo... aunque enfrente tendrá a un Villarreal que también llega necesitado de puntos. Favorito para el partido entre Málaga y Villarreal El conjunto castellonense cayó en su último compromiso frente al Betis, disputado en casa, y encadena ya tres derrotas consecutivas después de un comienzo de Liga sin victorias. El mal momento ha provocado, además, que comiencen a aparecer las primeras críticas hacia Iñigo Pérez, por lo que el duelo ante el Málaga adquiere una importancia especial para el técnico. Pese a todo, las casas de apuestas sitúan al Villarreal como favorito: 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.97 por su victoria, mientras que el triunfo local se paga a 3.64 y el empate, a 3.70. Ambos equipos marcan El primer mercado que analizamos dentro de las apuestas deportivas es el de ambos equipos marcan. Una opción que presenta argumentos a favor... pese a que el Málaga todavía no ha mostrado demasiada regularidad ofensiva. El conjunto andaluz ha cumplido este pronóstico en dos de sus cinco primeros encuentros, mientras que el Villarreal lo ha hecho en cuatro de cinco. Una tendencia que invita a esperar goles en ambas porterías. Además, la necesidad de victoria de los dos equipos puede favorecer un partido abierto y con alternativas. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.56 por el 'sí' y de 2.30 por el 'no'. Último equipo en marcar El Villarreal parte nuevamente con ventaja en este mercado, aunque sus números recientes no son especialmente contundentes. El Málaga ha conseguido marcar el último gol del encuentro en dos de sus cinco partidos, mientras que el conjunto castellonense solamente lo ha hecho en uno de sus cinco compromisos. Sin embargo, la mayor producción ofensiva que ha mostrado el equipo visitante hasta ahora hace que 1XBET le conceda el favoritismo. La cuota es de 1.68 si el Villarreal es el último en marcar, mientras que asciende hasta 2.36 en caso de que sea el Málaga quien cierre el marcador. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado del número total de goles presenta una clara diferencia entre las tendencias de ambos equipos. En los cinco primeros partidos del Málaga, solamente en uno se han superado los 2.5 tantos, mientras que el Villarreal ha visto más de 2.5 goles en cuatro de sus cinco encuentros. Esta estadística del conjunto castellonense, unida a la necesidad de ambos equipos de conseguir una victoria, puede apuntar hacia un duelo con varias ocasiones y un marcador por encima de la línea. 1XBET paga a 1.65 el 'más de 2.5 goles' y a 2.24 el 'menos de 2.5'.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: What should we believe from Week 1, for Week 2 and beyond?
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen highlights some surprising performance from Week 1, to see what they mean for the future.
articles.body:
I didn't decide to watch the TV show "Better Call Saul" until earlier this year. It was the offseason; I had free time, and it was long overdue. I loved "Breaking Bad", but I kept putting off watching Bob Odenkirk reprise his role as Saul Goodman because I already knew how it would end. I didn't need 63 episodes to tell me he was an immoral lawyer. But it's the "how" that got me hooked for six seasons (which I watched in about three weeks).

We just went through four days of NFL action. And in some cases, our box scores are telling us a convincing story. Whether good or bad, the results are final. We can't change where we wind up. However, the ancillary storylines may change our minds on whether we should believe Week 1 is indicative of what to expect for the rest of the season.

Of course, I was watching the Bengals game going on at the same time. But I had Parker Washington in a league and had over 10 PPR points midway through the first quarter.

There were five QBs to score more than 25.0 fantasy points. Trevor Lawrence was the only passer out of that group who didn't run for more than 50 yards or score using his legs. Only Josh Allen averaged more air yards per attempt (11.5 to 10.5). If there's anything to speak to the repeatability of Lawrence dismantling the Browns, it was the effortlessness of his high efficiency.

Passing Success Rate: 70.8%, 1st (among all Week 1 starters)

Completion Percentage Over Expected: +22.3%, 1st

Lawrence topped the lists of every advanced passing metric on just 23 attempts. That's the third-fewest of any QB to post similar numbers going back to 2020. He also had the "least help" from his receivers. At 3.4 YAC per reception, his depth and accuracy were more than enough to keep the Jaguars on schedule. But the sequencing is what will keep him in the top 10 discussion and have Chargers fans wishing the same was happening with their passer and playcaller.

On his second drive, Lawrence started in shotgun, threw two quick hitters to Brian Thomas Jr. and Washington, and then switched to the intermediate strikes on outbreakers. The two passes, resulting in a touchdown to Josh Cameron, came from under center play-action.

Sure, the Jaguars' ability to switch up and execute with any of their pass-catchers will have most managers frustrated week to week. But the production all intersects at Lawrence's right shoulder.

C.J. Stroud had one assignment coming into the year. Show us that the Divisional Round disaster was a fluke. And, on the whole, I'd say he passed the test.

Admittedly, losing two fumbles ( the second ending the game ) would sway anyone from my assessment. Houston needed its QB. He failed at the worst time. But Josh Allen almost did the same about 90 seconds earlier . Besides, the larger concern was whether Stroud could complete a forward pass after the last time we saw him.

Passing Success Rate: 51.2% (Week 1), 44.6% (2025)

I focused on obvious passing situations as Houston still relies on its running game on early downs. As a result, Stroud averaged 9.2 yards to go on third downs. But he still converted 42.9% of his attempts into a new series.

Stroud got pulled into a track meet against a former MVP, with only his WR1 and an unproven receiver corps behind him. With better matchups ahead (Colts, Cowboys, Titans), I'd bet on Stroud to be in the streaming discussion.

So, here's one way to frame Bucky Irving's Week 1. He only carried the ball eight times against a defense that finished 2025 allowing the third-most PPR PPG to RBs. Touchdowns are a strong deodorant for weak output. Plus, he couldn't keep his hands on the ball.

Again, that's one way you could look at Irving's trip to Cincinnati . The other paints a better, more sustainable picture.

Target Rate: 25.9%, 1st (out of all TB pass-catchers)

Seeing Irving as the RB1 wasn't a surprise. After Rachaad White 's departure and a healthy offseason, the starting job was as good as his. It was the fragility of the other parts of the job that warranted an ADP drop.

We considered Kenny Gainwell a direct threat after securing a 16% share in Pittsburgh last year. Nope. The former Eagle ran about half as many routes and earned just one target. Sure, Sean Tucker was inactive, but only Irving got the ball once the Bucs got into scoring position. With his workload looking more like his rookie season's, I'd expect bigger days from Irving in the coming weeks.

I've said it before, but fantasy production exists at the intersection of situation and talent. Unfortunately, I've got questions about both regarding MarShawn Lloyd.

I'll start with Lloyd's environment. Of course, it didn't help that his QB saw five or more rushers on an absurd 78.3% of his dropbacks . They had three drives with more than six plays. And Lloyd's position within the backfield wasn't much better.

Lloyd may have almost doubled Chris Brooks ' touch count, but all of his carries came on early downs. He ran fewer routes than Brooks and came off the field more often than the second-year rusher in the two-minute drill. And, as the above clip indicates, Lloyd did nothing to differentiate himself talent-wise.

Lloyd posted similar per-touch metrics as Brooks with twice as many opportunities. We may not know when (or if) Josh Jacobs will return to the lineup, but Lloyd's chances of being a reliable fantasy contributor already look bleak.

So, here's the good news about Jaylen Waddle's first game with the Broncos. First, he took the slot duties. He had his first 1,000-yard season as a rookie in Miami with a 60.1% slot snap rate.

Second, Waddle's receiving aDOT was 4.0 air yards. Bo Nix was fifth in EPA per dropback on short-area throws in '25. As we said all summer, the pairing was perfect. Apparently, it just needs time to mesh.

A key drop in an island game is a double whammy for Waddle, since more people were watching. The availability heuristic will have folks pointing back to that play for weeks. However, that's not the worst part of his debut.

You'd have to scroll past four other pass-catchers before you find Waddle's target total. And notice how I didn't specify a designation. Because if I say two WRs, an RB and a TE earned more looks than the guy Denver traded multiple picks to acquire, it sounds worse. Oh, and the Broncos' backup TE (University of Dayton's finest!) had the same number of targets.

The icing on the cake is neither Nix nor Davis Webb had an answer for DC Steve Spagnuolo's defense. Nix was under duress on 45.5% of his dropbacks. In long-down-and-distance situations, all of his throws were at or behind the LOS. And without a lesser opponent on the schedule for some time (at Carolina – Week 9), we're left to hope things change in a hurry.

But if I had Waddle on my roster, I'd look to other options on my team — or trade for reinforcements.

I can't win watching Bengals games. Because even if they walk away with a victory, there's at least one play that gives me another gray hair.

Two catches for 12 yards aren't what fantasy managers with the third overall pick signed up for each week. Even worse, this new look for the Bengals offense doesn't lean on its WRs as it has in years past.

RB Target Rate: 26.5% (2026), 17.0% (2025)

I like watching Mike Gesicki Griddy'ing in the end zone as much as the next person. But the veteran TE leading the entire receiver group breaks reality. Week 1 featured the second-lowest rate of passes thrown to a wide receiver in the Joe Burrow era (41.2%).

Regardless, at least for now, I'm not worried about No. 1. Nothing changed about Chase's on-field deployment. He was in the slot on 32.5% of his snaps. His route depth varied from deep go routes to quick hitches. And with all of the focus on Burrow using more under-center play-action, most will forget their only explosive from those looks came from a throw to Chase.

Give it time. Those two will find their rhythm soon.

I'm willing to wait until Thursday for Jameson Williams' breakout game.

Williams' first catch came within inches of crossing the scoring plane. But then, from drops to off-target throws, a promising start turned into a dud. However, it didn't stop Jared Goff from looking his way.

Williams led the Lions in air yards (54.2%), and only Amon-Ra St. Brown had more targets. And if Sunday was any indication, Detroit will have to keep up with every opponent as its defense struggles to limit yards.

Before Week 2's matchup start, try to trade for Williams.

Christian Watson is the embodiment of the " He Can't Keep Getting Away With It " meme. But it's fun to watch him do it.

My worry for Watson was that he wouldn't be able to take over some of the " Romeo Doubs " role. The Packers' WR1 accrued 48.1% of his yards last season on passes of 20 air yards or more. Fantasy managers need high valleys, not just high peaks. But even amidst the chaotic defensive approach, Watson wasn't just a downfield threat.

Half of his targets came in the short area of the field. Plus, with Matthew Golden taking the X-receiver looks, Watson could play off the LOS or in the slot. If Jordan Love has more time in the pocket, we'll likely see more deep shots. But to see this type of shift for Watson should boost our confidence about the ebbs and flows of his weekly receiver production.

articles.title: Mark Allen: Northern Ireland player prolongs absence with latest tournament withdrawal
articles.summary: Northern Ireland player Mark Allen prolongs his absence from competitive tournament snooker by withdrawing from the Shenzhen Open.
articles.body:
Mark Allen has prolonged his absence from professional tournament snooker by withdrawing from the forthcoming Shenzhen Open for personal reasons.

The event runs from 28 September to 4 October, with the Northern Ireland player having been scheduled to face Ben Mertens on the opening day in China.

World Snooker Tour last week confirmed that Allen would not participate in qualifiers for the International Championship.

The 40-year-old recently sat out the British and English Opens, meaning he had missed the first five ranking events of the season.

He also did not take part in the Championship League, China Open and Wuhan Open ranking events, plus the Shanghai Masters, which is a non-ranking tournament.

The world number 13 has not played in a professional event since losing to eventual winner Wu Yize in their World Championship semi-final at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield in early May.

The next tournament Allen is scheduled to compete in is his home event, the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast, from 18 to 25 October.

articles.title: The 10 Most Expensive Sports Memorabilia Items of All Time
articles.summary: Trading cards have become national news in recent years thanks to some high-profile sales landing well north of $1 million, but they are not the only pieces of sports memorabilia that can command an astronomical figure at auction.
articles.body:
Trading cards have become national news in recent years thanks to some high-profile sales landing well north of $1 million, but they are not the only pieces of sports memorabilia that can command an astronomical figure at auction.

Iconic jerseys of sports legends and various other sports equipment can also fetch a pretty penny, and just a few years ago a Babe Ruth jersey from the game of his famed "called shot" more than doubled the previous record sale for a piece of sports memorabilia.

The most expensive sports memorabilia items are a wide-ranging collection of sports history spanning baseball, basketball, soccer and even the Olympics.

Most memorable injury comebacks ahead of Mahomes return

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

10 MOST EXPENSIVE SPORTS MEMORABILIA ITEMS OF ALL TIME

Sale Price: $24,120,000 | Date: August 2024

There may be no more iconic moment in baseball history than Babe Ruth's called shot in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series, and while the debate rages on whether it actually happened, there is no doubt this is the jersey he was wearing in that game.

The jersey was originally acquired in 1990 from an elderly woman in Florida whose father was a golfing buddy of Ruth's and was gifted the jersey by him after his retirement. It sold for $940,000 in 2005, before it was verified to be from Game 3 specifically, and now it stands as the single most expensive piece of sports memorabilia of all time.

Sale Price: $10,091,100 | Date: September 2022

Estimated to fetch between $3-5 million by Sotheby's, Jordan's jersey from Game 1 of his last NBA Finals instead more than doubled that to briefly become the most valuable jersey sale of all-time. The Bulls actually lost Game 1 of those finals in overtime against the Utah Jazz, though Jordan dropped a game-high 33 points.

"A little with the head of Maradona, and a little with the hand of God."

Those famous words from Diego Maradona helped turn his handball goal in the 1986 World Cup quarterfinals against England into one of the most iconic moments in sports history.

The ball from that same play also recently sold at auction, fetching $3,355,000 in August 2026.

Sale Price: $8,806,500 | Date: December 2019

A 14-page speech from French aristocrat and educator Pierre de Coubertin to celebrate the fifth anniversary of the French Athletics Association culminated in a proposal to revive the ancient Olympic games. Two years later, the IOC was formed and the first modern games took place in Athens in 1896.

The only known copy of the speech was tracked down by French diplomat François d'Amat in the early 1990s in Switzerland after years of searching. Estimated to sell for between $700,000 and $1 million, it shattered expectations to become the most expensive piece of sports memorabilia at the time of the sale.

Sale Price: $8,032,800 | Date: February 2024

From the Sotheby's auction listing: "A set of 6 individual Air Jordan sneakers – each one worn by Michael Jordan in the clinching games of his 6 career NBA championships. The set consists of an Air Jordan VI (1991), Air Jordan VII (1992), Air Jordan VIII (1993), Air Jordan XI (1996), Air Jordan XII (1997), and Air Jordan XIV (1998)."

Jordan gave Bulls PR executive Tim Hallam a signed, game-worn sneaker following his first title in 1991, and continued the tradition after his subsequent five Finals-clinching games, thus creating this unique single-shoe collection.

Sale Price: $7,800,000 | Date: December 2023

Tech startup AC Momento, for which Lionel Messi is an investor, secured the first-half jerseys worn by Messi during the 2022 World Cup. They ended up with a collection of six jerseys, only excluding a group-stage match with Poland, and importantly centered around his World Cup final jersey when Messi scored twice and Argentina beat France.

A portion of the sale was donated to UNICAS Project, which focuses on children suffering from rare diseases.

Sale Price: $7,004,000 | Date: April 2025

The description doesn't quite do this one justice, as thanks to advanced photo matching technology, this jersey can be tied directly to his NBA media day, Bryant's preseason debut (Oct. 16, 1996), his regular-season debut (Nov. 3, 1996) and five other games from his rookie season.

The jersey previously sold for $115,242 at auction in 2012, making it the perfect snapshot of just how much growth has occurred in the high-end sports memorabilia market over the past decade-plus.

Sale Price: $6,180,000 | Date: July 2022

On October 30, 1974, Muhammad Ali knocked out the previously undefeated George Foreman to reclaim the world heavyweight championship in one of the most anticipated events in sports history, known as the "Rumble in the Jungle" with the fight taking place in Zaire, Africa.

Former Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay placed the winning bid.

Sale Price: $5,850,000 | Date: February 2023

The photo of Kobe Bryant tugging on his jersey while letting out a yell after hitting a clutch three-pointer in Game 2 of the 2008 Western Conference First Round against the Nuggets has become one of the enduring images of the Lakers superstar, and has in fact been immortalized in numerous murals across Los Angeles and the entire world.

This is the jersey he was wearing when he hit that shot, and it was worn in 25 total games, giving it an unusual level of action relative to most modern jerseys that are worn once.

Sale Price: $5,640,000 | Date: June 2019

In a live auction held at Yankee Stadium by Hunt Auctions, this Babe Ruth jersey set a new record at the time for the most expensive piece of sports memorabilia ever sold.

The previous record had also belonged to a Ruth jersey from the 1920 season, which sold for $4.4 million.

Comparing those figures to the sports card market, which has exploded into big business in recent years, three sports cards have topped the $10 million mark and eight sit above the $5 million threshold.

The 2007-08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Michael Jordan/Kobe Bryant Dual Logoman Auto that sold for $12,932,000 in August 2025 headlines that list, followed by a 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle SGC 9.5 that had been the record holder at $12,600,000 from an August 2022 sale.

For more on the absolute peak of the sports card market, check out: The 10 Most Expensive Sports Cards of All Time

articles.title: Stephanie White makes surprising Caitlin Clark admission after Team USA benching as Fever duo reunites
articles.summary: International Sports News: Caitlin Clark spent some time on the bench during the FIBA World Cup. Stephanie White watched every minute of it, and she came away with a different r.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark spent some time on the bench during the FIBA World Cup. Stephanie White watched every minute of it, and she came away with a different read than most fans did. Now that the two are back in Indiana with a gold medal in tow, White is putting her observations on record.Clark, a three-time WNBA All-Star, didn't crack the starting five for Team USA. According to her head coach, though, that supporting role did more for her game than a starting job might have. White's comments came right after a Fever practice, days before the team gets back to the business of chasing a WNBA title.Stephanie White reveals how Caitlin Clark has changed after Team USA benchingFans are used to seeing Caitlin Clark run an offense from the opening tip, not wait her turn. At the World Cup, she played behind veterans on a Team USA roster that went undefeated and closed things out with a gold-medal win over France. White, serving as an assistant under Kara Lawson, had a courtside seat for the entire transformation.Speaking with reporters, White broke down what stood out. She noticed Clark's pace shift the moment younger players entered games, and she pointed to the jump from WNBA basketball to international competition as a teaching tool in itself.“You could tell the way that she was able to change the game with her pace, and how, when we put our young guns in there, it looked a little bit different. I think for C, being able to learn from those veterans, FIBA is different,” White shared.She added, “World Cup and Olympics is different. It’s not the WNBA. And having that experience with those guys, I think she’s able to learn by watching. I think she felt the difference in different games and how teams are going to play, what she’s looking for. I thought her floor game was outstanding.”The clearest proof came in the final against France, when Clark knocked down a shot right before halftime that swung momentum toward the Americans. "So I'm really proud of her," White said. Not everyone loved watching a franchise centerpiece ride the pine on the international stage, but if White's assessment holds up, that stretch of games may end up paying off for Indiana down the stretch.The Indiana Fever are back in the gameNow, White, Clark, and forward Aliyah Boston are back with the Fever, and the reunion had real emotion behind it inside the practice facility. Forward Myisha Hines-Allen made no secret of who she wanted to see first. "First person I saw was AB (Aliyah Boston)." Hines-Allen said, before wrapping her in a hug.White wasted no time resetting expectations. Fatigue from a demanding international stretch isn't an excuse, in her view, and the standard for this group doesn't bend just because legs are heavy. To smooth the transition, Clark and Boston sat out practice on their first day back, and White eased her own way back into the fold as well. Hines-Allen gave credit to the rest of the roster for keeping intensity up while the trio was overseas, noting that the group never let up in their absence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Maple Leafs face new Auston Matthews concern as ESPN analyst raises questions about lingering effects from his knee injury
articles.summary: NHL News: Auston Matthews is heading into a pivotal season for the Toronto Maple Leafs, and now there's a new wrinkle to watch. ESPN analyst Ray Ferraro used hi.
articles.body: Auston Matthews is heading into a pivotal season for the Toronto Maple Leafs, and now there's a new wrinkle to watch. ESPN analyst Ray Ferraro used his own injury history to raise doubts about whether Matthews has fully bounced back from his knee troubles. Speaking on TSN's OverDrive alongside Bryan Hayes, Jeff O'Neill and Jamie McLennan, Ferraro didn't hold back. The conversation also touched on Matthews' next contract, with Hayes and Ferraro landing in very different places on what the star center is worth right now.What did Ray Ferraro say about Auston Matthews' health?Ferraro drew from personal experience when talking about Matthews. He recalled his own knee surgeries and how camp-ready confidence sometimes gave way to reality once the games actually started counting. "I know you guys have had injuries that have lingered from one year to the next. And oftentimes it takes you a while; even though you feel pretty good, you're like, you're just not quite right for a while," he said.He wasn't done there. Ferraro added a more personal layer, drawing directly from what he went through during his playing days. "And I don't know if that's the case. You know, I just know with the knee trouble that I had and the surgeries I had, I always felt like I was ready to go, and then in September, October, I'm like, wow, I don't quite feel like I think I should feel. And maybe there'll be some of that too."That's a fair warning for Leafs fans hoping Matthews looks like his old self from day one. Ferraro went further, noting the overall uncertainty surrounding the franchise. "I would say there are more unknowns around the Leafs than there have been in quite some time," he said, and that comment alone says a lot about where things stand in Toronto right now.How does Auston Matthews' health tie into his next contract?Money entered the discussion too. Hayes argued that fifteen million might actually undersell Matthews if he puts together a strong 2026-27 campaign. Ferraro pushed back, pointing out that kind of money would come easily elsewhere "for fun," given Matthews' pedigree. Still, Hayes raised a sharper question: after two down years and major surgery, does a third disappointing season mean his prime has already passed? Ferraro wasn't ready to go that far, but he didn't dismiss the contractual stakes either.None of this settles anything before puck drop. But it does frame the season ahead differently. Every shift Matthews takes early on will now be watched a little closer, not just for production, but for signs of how his body is actually holding up.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Women’s sports bar's hypocrisy shows as it disavows the very thing it was meant to support | Matt Calkins
articles.summary: The Sports Bra in Portland kicked out customers wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts and boycotted Women's Elite Rugby over its trans athlete policy.
articles.body: We know that, at some point, the Sports Bra was a Portland bar built for broadcasting women's sports. One can assume that, at some point, it would show WNBA or NWSL or Women's World Cup games on its screens. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's unclear, however, how often gymnastics would be displayed. But the owner seems to be doing a lot of them in her head. The Pacific Northwest establishment first came under national scrutiny after it expelled a group of fans for wearing XX-XY Athletics T-shirts earlier in the month. Video shows a server telling the group that their attire was making other customers uncomfortable, and that despite them already having ordered their food, they had to leave. This spawned a social-media firestorm, with myriad X users condemning the bar for its not-so-inclusive behavior. And upon a deeper look, it's uncertain how much the Sports Bra cares about women's sports at all. As XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey pointed out earlier in the week, the bar has a history of activism that goes beyond chucking customers for their garb. Earlier this summer, it announced a boycott of all Women's Elite Rugby matches. The reason? The rugby league said it would follow USOPC policy in disallowing transgender athletes from participating. In short: the women's sports bar banned a women's sport because it wouldn't allow men to play. "We're doing this in solidarity with the players, fans, and organizers calling for rugby to live up to its own values of respect, integrity and inclusion," a bar representative posted on Instagram. "The Sports Bra exists to celebrate and elevate women and girls in sports. That includes trans women and girls. Always. We love women's sports. We love seeing new leagues grow. We want more athletes on bigger stages with more fans in the stands. But growth cannot come at the cost of belonging." OutKick reached out to the Sports Bra for comment, but did not get a reply as of publication time. One thing I wanted to know is what their requirement for streaming any sport was. After all, the NCAA, WTA, Olympics and FIBA all adhere to the same USOPC policy, which would seem to mirror the Rugby league policy. There isn't a whole lot left after that, besides the WNBA, at least for now. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Second, where on Earth was anybody going to find Women's Elite Rugby matches save for a place like the Sports Bra? You're not going to see that at the Yard House or Buffalo Wild Wings. All this boycott did was limit the already scarce number of eyeballs that would have been on a niche women's sport. Who exactly benefits from this? The answer: People who want to feel a sense of moral superiority under the guise of "inclusion." The hard left's treatment of women is fascinating to me. Having worked at the Seattle Times for 11 years, I felt like I saw the term "toxic masculinity" every time I logged onto our website. We had one writer who declared unequivocally that, because of various crime and domestic violence stats, she would prefer to be alone with a bear over a man. And yet, as soon as that man declares he's a woman he achieves instance reverence. Suddenly, the women are the oppressor group. Suddenly, their concern about competing against a biological male or sharing a locker room with them is chalked up to bigotry. It comes down to a victimhood hierarchy, in which whoever is considered to be more marginalized gets the support — logic or fairness be damned. The truth is, sports are not typically about "inclusion." They're really more about exclusion. Only so many people make the team, get to start, run in the final heat, or earn a scholarship. The vast majority of athletes are denied the role or position they want to be in. This is the driving force behind competition. Of course, none of this means that one should lack compassion for people who feel confused or trapped in the wrong body. But you can do this while also acknowledging an unmistakable biological advantage that has led to various trans athletes winning high school, college and professional championships. The most vocal left-wing activists don't want to do that. The folks at the Sports Bra don't seem to want to, either. They're too busy bouncing customers and boycotting games. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Funny, when the bar opened four years ago, it seemed like it was one of women's sports biggest champions. Now? It may just be one of women's sports biggest enemies.

articles.title: Can Brad Marchand overcome injury concerns before Florida Panthers begin their NHL title defence
articles.summary: NHL News: Brad Marchand is recovering from surgery ahead of the Florida Panthers' 2026-27 NHL season. Will he return in time for the opener against the Carolina Hurricanes?
articles.body: The Florida Panthers will open the 2026-27 NHL season with Brad Marchand as the veteran forward continues to recover from surgery in August. On Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026, when the team opened training camp in Fort Lauderdale, general manager Bill Zito confirmed the news.Marchand has been dealing with injury issues with his hip and sports hernia for months now. Reports indicate the Panthers are taking a cautious approach and not rushing the 38-year-old forward back into competitive action, although he has returned to skating. articles.title: Baker Mayfield sends blunt message on Buccaneers facing former team
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield comes clean on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers facing his former team, the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be looking to get in the win column in Week 2 against the Cleveland Browns .

The Buccaneers pulled off a gusty effort on the road in Week 1 against the Cincinnati Bengals , but they came up short in their 33-27 loss. A lot of that had to do with their four fumbles, including three alone by Baker Mayfield. Those turnovers directly led to 17 points for the Bengals, which obviously proved to be the difference for Cincinnati.

As the Buccaneers prepare for their home opener against the Browns, the game is also notable because it represents Mayfield's former franchise. Mayfield began his career as the Browns' No. 1 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft and spent the first four seasons in Cleveland (2018-2021), helping lead the Team to its first playoff win since 1994.

As he and the team prepare for their game against the Browns, Mayfield downplayed the storyline about him and instead focused on winning the next game.

"I mean, obviously, there's history there — there's no way to go around that," Mayfield said of the upcoming game against his former team. "It's the next opponent. Cleveland happens to be the next opponent — our home opener. So, yeah. Have a bad taste in our mouth, looking forward to getting it out."

"It's still the next one, and that's the most important one," Mayfield continued. "I've said that to you guys over the years — it doesn't matter who it is, the most important one is the next one. And we've got — I've got to get some stuff fixed. And we've got to move forward."

The Browns were thumped in their season opener, 34-10, against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It'll be their second consecutive game on the road in Florida, and it won't be an easy task considering the Buccaneers will be hungry for their first win after coming up a little short in Week 1.

Even head coach Todd Bowles downplayed the meaning of Mayfield facing his former team during media availability on Monday.

"No, I don't think so," said Bowles on if it will affect his play. "Baker is a very smart guy. He understands that he has to play better and take care of the football. That comes first, and then we'll worry about the opponent."

While the Browns are a completely different team since Mayfield last suited up for them in 2021, given how competitive the veteran quarterback is, he'll likely be looking for any extra motivation to win in Week 2. Considering he's facing his former team, who let him go in favor of Deshaun Watson, the Browns' Week 2 starter, it's safe to say that Mayfield will be playing with a chip on his shoulder come this Sunday.

articles.title: 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling out about 10 weeks with deltoid rupture
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling is out about 10 weeks after having surgery for a deltoid rupture.

Despite winning their season opener by 20 points, the San Francisco 49ers suffered a significant blow in their season opener against the Los Angeles Rams . Rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, a preseason standout for the 49ers, will miss about 10 weeks with a deltoid rupture.

The original timeline for Stribling was about a month. However, after seeking other opinions, Stribling and the 49ers decided to fully repair the deltoid rupture. He is expected to make a full recovery.

If he misses exactly 10 weeks, he will return for San Francisco 's game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 22. If it were a little longer, he could come back in time for their December matchup against the New York Giants.

Stribling was expected to play a major role in the 49ers' offense this season. Now, San Francisco will need other receivers, such as Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel , to keep making an impact this season. Both receivers were targeted seven times, had six receptions, and caught a touchdown in the season opener. Running back Christian McCaffrey also played an active role in the receiving game with eight targets and five receptions.

articles.title: Eagles players who could create momentum in Week 2 vs. Titans
articles.summary: Here are a handful of Eagles stars and an up-and-comers who can use Week 2 as an opportunity to build confidence and momentum.
articles.body:
Days have passed, and people are still talking about the Philadelphia Eagles escaping Week 1 with a victory. As is often the case in the NFL, the result was more important than the style points. There were encouraging moments. There were frustrating moments. Most importantly, plenty of room remains for growth.

That shouldn't shock anyone. That is often the case early in the regular season.

September is often when players settle into roles, units develop chemistry, and confidence begins to build. One strong performance can change a narrative. One productive afternoon can create momentum that carries into the rest of the season.

As the Eagles travel to Nashville for a Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans , Philadelphia will be favored . Several players and position groups have an opportunity to take an important step forward.

Week 1 wasn't the type of performance Eagles fans have come to expect from Cooper DeJean . He battled through some adversity and wasn't quite as impactful as usual.

The good news is that the NFL schedule doesn't allow players much time to dwell on a rough outing. Vic Fangio remains confident . Tennessee's receiving corps has talent, but the Titans are still searching for consistency at quarterback.

If DeJean can return to playing fast and instinctive football, Week 2 could provide an opportunity to regain some confidence. He should remind everyone why he has become such an important piece of Philadelphia's defense.

DeVonta Smith remains one of the most polished route runners in football, and Philadelphia knows it. Unfortunately, Smith wasn't a major focal point for stretches of the opener.

That could change quickly against Tennessee. The Titans are coming off a difficult defensive performance against the New York Jets , and the Eagles should have opportunities to attack through the air. If Tennessee devotes extra attention elsewhere, Smith could be in line for a much larger afternoon.

Chris Kuper and the Eagles' offensive line

This isn't about one player so much as an entire unit looking to build momentum. The offensive line did not perform up to its usual standard in Week 1, and now it faces another challenge with Landon Dickerson heading to injured reserve .

That creates an opportunity for Chris Kuper's group to show its resilience. Philadelphia's offense works best when the running game controls the tempo, and Jalen Hurts operates from a clean pocket. A stronger showing in Nashville would go a long way toward restoring confidence in a unit that expects much more from itself.

The Eagles are still learning exactly how much Mukuba can give them, but the early signs remain encouraging. Philadelphia's defense would certainly welcome a few extra possessions while the offense continues to find its rhythm.

That's where Mukuba's instincts and playmaking ability become valuable. Whether it's breaking up a pass, forcing a turnover, or capitalizing on a mistake, he has the skill set to swing momentum quickly.

The Eagles remain confident in Makai Lemon's future, and there is no reason for that to change after one week. Young receivers often need time, opportunities, and a few successful moments to get rolling.

Nashville could give Lemon a chance to start building that confidence. Nobody expects him to become a featured target suddenly. Still, a couple of meaningful plays could build momentum and reinforce the belief that he can become a valuable contributor as the season unfolds.

Momentum can come in many forms. Sometimes it's a breakout performance. Other times it's a player regaining confidence, earning additional opportunities, or simply taking another step forward.

The Eagles have plenty of stars who can carry the spotlight. Week 2, however, may be remembered for what happens around them. If DeJean, Smith, Mukuba, Lemon, and Philadelphia's offensive line build on their opportunities, the Eagles could leave Nashville with more than a win. They could leave with several important pieces moving in the right direction.

articles.title: 5 Burning Questions heading into Avalanche training camp
articles.summary: Let the games begin!
articles.body:
It's here, the new hockey sesson has arrived!

But first, before the games are played, every contracted player in the organization must gather for three days of training camp and for four preseason games before the 2026-27 season drops the puck on September 30th. Here is the expected roster comprised of 56 players hoping to make the Colorado Avalanche roster.

The biggest storyline on the new season concerns all the young forwards who could make the opening night roster. But before we get to that point, I'm keeping an eye on their usage at camp and in preseason. Of course the period before the games count is time for experimentation and no line or role is set in stone. Still, there are a lot of hints offered on how the organization views a player by how they are utilized in training camp. We'll find out their place on day one of on-ice activity.

On the opposite side of the spectrum, it will be fascinating to see the early thoughts on how to utilize the incoming veterans, Jaden Schwartz and the first full season of the second Nazem Kadri era, in particular. The assumption is Schwartz was brought in to help anchor Brock Nelson 's line, which would likely lend Kadri to center the third line. If those assumptions are incorrect then we'll see what Jared Bednar has in mind for his line construction.

Attendance has been strong at captain's skates but there's always a few curiosities leading to health questions. Cale Makar had been easing in and skating on his own away from the group for the most part. Jared Bednar remarked in his opening press conference that Makar is dealing with a new lower-body injury and might not participate right away in camp. Nathan MacKinnon was missing for all pre-camp gatherings but did skate with his teammates once two days before the start of training camp. Bednar said there was a handful of lingering issues from the offseason so attendance at camp might be an interesting topic to follow.

How will the shortened camp make an impact?

This is the first fall under the NHL's new Collective Bargaining Agreement, which has increased the regular season slate by two games to 84. In exchange, preseason was shortened by a week and reduced to a maximum of four exhibition games. Will we see an Avalanche squad full of older veterans rejuvenated due to this extra rest or will they stumble out of the gate with a lack of cohesive preparation? Gauging energy and cohesion will be an early temperature check.

This one isn't just for the Colorado Avalanche with the Lumberyard duo of Mackenzie Blackwood and Scott Wedgewood as the Colorado Eagles have their very own interesting tandem set for this season with the entrenched Trent Miner and top prospect Ilya Nabokov now in the fold. I'm watching to see how their playing time is split especially with the lessened opportunity to get in just the four exhibition games. Four solid goalies in an organization is a good problem to have but the aim is probably to have a starter for each team identified by puck drop on the regular season.

What do you want to hear about from training camp? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: The menu release is here for famous Bills tailgate
articles.summary: Tailgating is so important to the vibe at Bills games, and this is my favorite spot
articles.body:
Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team.

And I'm writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I've been friends with Rory and Ray since Kindergarten and have remained close friends with these brothers through a lot with the Bills over the years.

It's a bond that has always extended beyond Bills tailgates, but as we've gotten older, the Bills tailgates have become our central meeting ground, a guaranteed place to reconvene every fall and winter. And I sincerely cherish the yearly regathering with these two.

I'm sure you know the exact feeling of camaraderie with your tailgating group.

What started as a nano-tailgate with a deep fryer for wings and fries has gradually morphed into a full-scale tailgating operation, often feeding 50-plus patrons thanks to multiple flat tops, cooking apparatuses, and condiments galore. I cannot recommend the Parker Brothers Tailgate enough.

And here is their menu for the 2026 Bills season.

(Rory and Ray will be situated in the new "white" lot — behind Prohibition 2020 — for the 2026 campaign, and they welcome you to join them.)

Week 2 – September 17: Detroit Lions, 8:15pm — Birria tacos

This was a new menu item in 2025, and it went over like gangbusters. And who hasn't experienced the birria taco craze at their local Mexican restaurant or taqueria?

Well the Parkers are bringing that succulent experience to the grand opening of the new Highmark Stadium. Slow-cooked, marinated beef, melted Oaxacan cheese, and a consomé that knocks your socks off the moment you take your first bite.

Birria tacos will hit the spot on a momentous evening in Orchard Park with weather that should still feel like summer… before literal and figurative fireworks inside the new stadium.

Week 3 – September 27: Los Angeles Chargers — No tailgate (wedding in Lake George)

For the first time I can remember, Rory and Ray will not be at a Bills tailgate, working tirelessly to feed the masses before unwinding while watching their Bills play. Family wedding in the Adirondacks will keep them away for this one, but trust me, they'll be back with more energy than ever after their own bye week.

Week 4 – October 4: New England Patriots, 1pm — Stingers

What wings are to Buffalo, stinger subs are to the Parkers tailgate. Well, stingers and garbage plates.

Every year, the stinger tailgate attracts more friends and random passers-by than any other because of the Parkers' attention to detail with their stinger construction.

Thick chicken fingers, dipped in country sweet sauce, combined with perfectly cooked shredded beef, with any combination of lettuce, cheese, onions, banana peppers, and mayo on a fresh sub roll that can be toasted if you'd like (highly recommend it).

All ahead of a colossal showdown with the defending AFC champs in the House That Josh Built.

Week 8 – November 1: Baltimore Ravens, 1pm — Surprise, Surprise

Despite the pestering of my Parker Brothers sources, this tailgate remains a mystery. All I could manage to coax from said source was this, and it's awesomely cryptic, it's actually making me hungry right now:

"This tailgate has never been done before, maybe never again," and "I'll go out on a limb and say no one has ever tried it ever."

….as if you needed more encouragement to get to Bills-Ravens.

Week 11 – November 22: Miami Dolphins, 1pm — Turkey 2 Ways

If the answer is no, this is one glorious sliver of life you have yet to experience.

The Parkers call this Turkey 2 Ways because you can get a few slices of classically cooked Thanksgiving turkey. And if that's your jam, I respect that.

I recommend a taste of the Parkers deep-fried version that of course features a crunchy exterior and impossibly juicy meat as the focal point around mashed potatoes, corn, and everything else you'll eventually eat on Thanksgiving with your family.

Week 12 – November 26: Kansas City Chiefs, 8:20pm — Cheesesteaks

Why aren't the Parkers doing a Thanksgiving tailgate on Thanksgiving night? Well, they figured the tryptophan would probably be overwhelming at this stage of Thanksgiving, so they're venturing away from all the food you've likely eaten in the hours leading up to this perennial enormous regular-season battle between the Bills and Chiefs.

And the Parkers Cheesesteaks could hold their own on any corner on the streets of Philadelphia. Trust me. Ask for extra cheese. Thank me later.

Week 15 – December 19: Chicago Bears — Italian beef

A cousin of the Cheesesteaks, I actually slightly prefer the Italian beef — my last name should be a dead giveaway I'd have this take.

Of course, this menu item from Rory and Ray is a nod to one of Chicago's most revered culinary offerings, which just so happens to be the city's version of the beef on weck.

The spicy giardiniera — finely diced peppers, carrots, celery — elevate this sandwich into the stratosphere. And the warm, seasoned roast beef will warm your insides ahead of this super-fun AFC-NFC showdown between two of the best improvisational quarterbacks in the NFL.

Week 18 – January 10: New York Jets, TBD — Smash burgers

I adore smash burgers, and every time I eat one, I wonder… how and why were we not always eating burgers this way… two patties, pressed thin, with ample amounts of melted cheese to hold them together?

And the Parkers have perfected the on-site smash burger… Ray is normally on the flat-top, precisely flattening each patty before loading with cheese.

Rory's responsibilities come in the made-to-order building of your burger. And he will walk you through the process once your patties are ready to be assembled between two buns.

Because the Parkers have gotten so good with the presentation — and taste — of their smash burgers, this is an exquisite cap to the Bills 2026 regular season at this tailgate.

Among the menu items the Parkers have done in the past that would be possible during a Bills playoff run:

Garbage Plates (unequivocally my favorite, thanks in large part to Mrs. Parker's meat sauce)

Hibachi (a gigantic undertaking but Michelin-star worthy)

Burritos (made to your exact specifications, Chipotle-style)

Breakfast (bacon, sausage, eggs, all sizzling on the griddle)

Deep-fried everything (bring anything you want, the Parkers will deep fry right in front of your eyes)

Spaghetti and meatballs (I never knew I needed this Italian classic before a football game, until I went to a Parker Tailgate)

What is your tailgate scene like? Are you already planned out with specific menu items? Leave a comment explaining everything in detail!

Speaking with State Farm, she revealed how she idolised the Philadelphia 76ers star growing up.

She said: "I don't get starstruck too often. I try to play it cool. But probably when I met LeBron, that's the person that I grew up idolising."

The two icons officially linked up in person in March 2025, meeting in Indianapolis following a Lakers road game against the Pacers .

Clark has since reflected on how their connection has evolved since that first face-to-face conversation. She noted that James has been an incredible source of backing, emphasizing that he truly understands the intense public scrutiny and constant spotlight she navigates every day.

articles.title: Kentucky at Texas A&M: Week three defensive X Factors
articles.summary: We take a look at defensive X factors for Kentucky and Texas A&M that can make an impact on Saturday.
articles.body:
Kentucky football faces their first road game of the season as they will be in front of a hostile crowd in College Station to take on Texas A&M . We have previewed the Aggies defense , and what the Wildcats offense will be up against on Saturday. Both of these defense have looked like the better side of the football through two weeks, and we could be in for a defensive battle this weekend. Let's take a look at the X factors on the defense that can make an impact in this game.

We talked all offseason how the scheme change on defense could be extremely beneficial to edge defender Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace. Against Alabama , we saw that play out as Humphrey-Grace created issues for the Crimson Tide offensive line. The pick six was an unbelievable play from the 6'4, 270-pound edge. He also had a sack and 1.5 tackles for loss in the week two loss, but Humphrey-Grace is a football player that will put a ton of stress on this unproven Texas A&M offensive line.

Another player that will be problematic for the Texas A&M offensive line is defensive tackle Tavion Gadson. Gadson was another player we said would benefit from the scheme change and is a guy the NFL has a close eye on. We also saw that play out against Alabama, as Gadson had 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and a pass deflection. Gadson is a powerful three technique with long arms that can overwhelm interior offensive lineman.

Ty Bryant is the returning leader of this defense, and he has kept the momentum going from his incredible 2025 season. Safety Jordan Castell has made a ton of plays through two weeks, and this safety tandem has proven to be a strength of this defense. Bryant needs to use his ball hawking ability we saw last season and create a turnover on Saturday. This is a game where turnovers could really amplify things for either team, and quarterback Marcel Reed has been known to put the ball in harms way at times.

The Aggies have one of the best safeties in the conference as well with Marcus Ratcliffe. Ratcliffe has eight tackles and a pass breakup on the season. He is the leader of an extremely talented secondary for Mike Elko. Elko will do a lot of what Jay Bateman does, given Bateman was his defensive coordinator for two seasons before coming to Lexington; they will rotate this safeties pre-snap and post-snap to try and confuse opposing quarterbacks.

DJ Hicks is one of the best defensive tackles in the SEC, and does a lot of work that doesn't show up in the stat sheet. Hicks is 6'3, 293-pounds and is great at stopping the run, which could really slow down the Wildcats running game. Kentucky has to get the run game going better than they did last week against Alabama, and Hicks is the best player that can slow that down. Kentucky's interior offensive line has to create movement up front to open up holes for the running backs, this is a key area to keep an eye on this Saturday.

New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson has launched a new brand advisory firm, Thirty Third Management Group, with his family to manage his off-court business. Focus Financial Partners is serving as financial advisor to Brunson, his family and the new firm.

In addition to managing Brunson's off-court business, Thirty Third Management Group will also represent clients across professional sports, business and philanthropy. Erica Brunson, Jalen's sister and director of client services, will lead the firm's initiative focused on women's professional sports, an underserved area.

Sandra Brunson, his mother, will serve as president of Thirty Third, which represents Jalen Brunson's NBA draft pick in 2018. Connor Cashaw, a former professional basketball player who has been a part of Jalen's team since 2025, has been appointed director of business development.

"My family has been with me every step of the way, and everything we do is rooted in trust," Jalen Brunson said in a statement. "Thirty Third gives us the chance to take ownership of my off-court business, to build something that reflects who we are, and to do it together."

"We are committed to helping our clients maximize opportunities, whether in professional sports, business, or philanthropy, and want to be a strategic partner that champions both success and significance," Erica Brunson said in a statement.

In June, the New York Knicks won their first NBA championship in 53 years. Jalen was unanimously named the Bill Russell NBA Finals Most Valuable Player.

The team was awarded more than $9 million, and it has been a win not only for Focus. Goldman Sachs' wealth management business also counts some of the Knicks players as clients, according to Bloomberg .

Matt Kennedy, a 6-foot-2 Villanova University graduate who spent years as a teammate of Knicks players Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges, is on that Goldman Sachs team.

On X (formerly Twitter), Jalen Brunson confirmed that he was a wealth management client of Kennedy's.

articles.title: Real Madrid fan group demands Mbappe apology for Ceuta shirt snub
articles.summary: Mbappe, Vinicius Jr and Ibrahima Konate wore a tribute shirt partially rolled up ahead of Madrid’s 3-2 win at Elche.
articles.body:
A Real Madrid supporters’ group has demanded a public apology from Kylian Mbappe and two teammates after they declined to fully wear a T-shirt in support of the people of Ceuta.

Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Ibrahima Konate wore a tribute shirt partially rolled up ahead of Madrid’s 3-2 win at Elche on Tuesday in La Liga.

“We are certain that every Real Madrid supporter and every Spaniard is ashamed of the image given by these three individuals,” Ultras Sur said in a statement posted on X late on Wednesday, describing their conduct as “unacceptable”.

The group, which is often associated with the far-right, called for “public apologies” and criticised the silence of Real Madrid President Florentino Perez, with whom it has been at odds since being banned from the Santiago Bernabeu more than a decade ago.

La Liga President Javier Tebas on Wednesday criticised the three Madrid players for not properly wearing the T-shirt, saying “putting it half on is the same as not wearing it”.

The rest of the team and Elche players wore the T-shirt properly. It brandished the words “we are all Ceutans”, intended to be a message of support for people in the Spanish territory in North Africa recently affected by a migration crisis .

Residents have complained about migrants from Morocco camping on beaches and sleeping in the streets, with the city overwhelmed amid a humanitarian crisis. Scores of people died while attempting the crossing in July.

The Moroccan Association for Human Rights, a nongovernmental group, estimates at least 141 died.

Mbappe said that he wanted to make a gesture in support of those who had lost their lives.

“The first thing I want to say is that I have complete solidarity with Ceuta and all the victims,” he told the Spanish daily sports newspaper, AS.

“But I also wanted to make a gesture and express my thoughts for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in difficult conditions.”

Tens of thousands of migrants arrived in Ceuta from Morocco on July 30 and 31 .

Most returned hours after they arrived, but several thousand remained in Ceuta, where deteriorating conditions have fuelled tensions with local residents.

articles.title: Watch this: The winning timepieces you couldn't miss at this year's US Open
articles.summary: The US Open has become a must-see event for luxury watch fans eager to spot who's wearing what. Quaid Walker, CEO of the watch marketplace Bezel, picks out t...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev may now well be mulling over that old saying that time heals all wounds. Four years ago he faced a lengthy time off-court after horrifically tearing his ankle ligaments during the French Open semi-final match against Rafael Nadal. This year's not over yet but it's undoubtedly been the most successful period of the German tennis champion's career as he celebrates lifting two Grand Slam titles.

On Sunday night as he lifted the US Open trophy in New York, Zverev had one eye on the time back on the old continent too, as he brandished a Jacob & Co "The World Is Yours" Dual Time Zone Tourbillon — a piece with two sub-dials for a second time zone.

Luxury watch brands have been competing hard to be in the winner's photo for decades, and the final at Flushing Meadows is no exception. "The Open gets covered as a watch-spotting event in its own right", says Quaid Walker, CEO of Bezel , one of the world's leading platforms for buying and selling luxury watches.

"Zverev played the tournament in a skeletonized Epic X on an elastic band and changed into this for the trophy, which has become a small ritual of sorts among players with watch sponsorships."

"The point of the swap is to be seen, and few watches are built to be seen like this one, with a globe-shaped dial and a tourbillon running at its center. It's a sight to behold, which is essentially the whole idea", adds Walker.

The watch's globe-shaped dial is detailed right down to the mountain ranges and coastlines. At its centre, a so-called 30-second tourbillon spins twice as fast as a standard one — and it made waves last year at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève .

Alcaraz brings out the collector's holy grail

Even though it did not lift the cup, Rolex — official watchmaker of the four Grand Slams and by far the watch brand most assossiated to tennis — stole the show during the entire event. The Spanish defending champion Carlos Alcaraz crossed the Atlantic wearing the Rolex Daytona "Le Mans," launched to mark the 100th anniversary of the French endurance race in 2023.

That "100" printed in red on the black Cerachrom bezel is enough to send collectors into a frenzy — the watch now fetches over €200,000 on the second-hand market.

"Even when it was in production, you likely couldn't get your hands on one. These went exclusively to the brand's most established clients, with sub-single-year production runs per metal prior to discontinuation", Walker recalls.

The brand with the crown signed the Spaniard in January 2022, just months before he won his first Grand Slam title at the US Open aged 19 and became the youngest player to ever top the ATP ranking. His comeback, however, from a troublesome wrist injury lay off was halted when he was narrowly beaten in the semis by home favourite Ben Shelton.

Although Shelton went on to lose in the final against Zverev, he cemented his place as one of Rolex's newest crown jewels alongside the brand's roster of "Testimonees" which now includes former US Open winners Jannik Sinner, Coco Gauff, and of course Roger Federer .

The Swiss tennis legend, who retired in 2022, was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame during this year's US Open, and chose the prestigious occasion to sport Rolex's latest, most colourful creation, the Oyster Perpetual 41 "Jubilee" — one of the most hyped watches of 2026.

"Since around 2020, the dial has overwhelmingly influenced the value of an Oyster Perpetual. The original lacquer colors did it first, the Celebration motif pushed it further, and the Jubilee is its most extreme version yet, with ten colours pad-printed in sequence. It's undeniably the OP to have right now, a fact reinforced by its presence on Federer's wrist," says Walker.

Vekić and Kostyuk bring independents courtside

Two women players really let their wrist do the talking at the tournament. When Croatia's Donna Vekić was knocked out in the second round by world number 29 Ann Li, she was wearing an FP Journe — one of the most sought-after independent brands among watchonistas.

The titanium Elégante's electromechanical movement has a quirky trick: it stops ticking when at rest, then wakes itself up and resets to the correct time the moment it senses movement on your wrist. That gives it remarkable battery life — 8 to 10 years with daily wear.

Another eye-catching piece was a Patek Philippe Aquanaut Luce as blue as the Flushing Meadows' acrylic hard courts. This 36mm steel watch, its bezel set with 46 diamonds, was worn by Marta Kostyuk.

Kostyuk was knocked out in the fourth round, but still walked away with a major milestone to celebrate. The Ukrainian will break into the WTA Top 10 on Monday, joining her compatriot Elina Svitolina in making Ukrainian tennis history.

Up in the stands, brands made the most of the tournament to put on a show. "The Open is three weeks of tennis in New York, and the good seats are on camera for hours at a stretch. No other American sporting event gives you that kind of sustained view of who's there and what they're wearing. What ends up on a wrist in those seats is a decision now," notes Walker.

Among the standout pieces: model Kaia Gerber wore a Cartier Panthère in yellow gold, in its "mini" size — a watch that costs roughly 100 times less than the RM 75-01 Flying Tourbillon Sapphire sported by rapper Travis Scott, estimated at more than €2 million.

"Scott has his own Audemars Piguet, a brown ceramic Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar he designed with the brand in 2023, so it says something that this is what he reached for instead. A sapphire-cased flying tourbillon is the brand at its most technical and least apologetic," according to Walker.

The Flying Tourbillon, a hallmark of Richard Mille, was incarnated in the tennis world by Rafael Nadal, who wore it during his final appearance at Roland-Garros in 2024.

Actor Brad Pitt, meanwhile, turned up wearing one of Swiss watchmaking's true classics: the Patek Philippe reference 2526, Calatrava model, valued at between €200,000 and €350,000 on the second-hand market.

"The 2526 houses Patek Philippe's first automatic caliber, the 12-600AT, which is still held in high regard. Its reputation rests as much on the design, where enamel against warm gold produces a delicate quality that's tough to beat. That same enamel doesn't forgive age or poor service, so clean examples have thinned considerably over 70 years. It's great to see one being worn on a bracelet rather than tucked away in a safe", Walker concludes.

Victory or not, one thing is clear: at the US Open, there are many winners being worn on wrists.

articles.title: Leicestershire handed huge points deduction as Bollywood film shoot blamed for damaged pitch
articles.summary: Leicestershire beat Glamorgan last month but have now been docked all of the points from their victory
articles.body:
Leicestershire face the prospect of relegation after being handed a 27-point deduction over the substandard condition of their pitch, despite claims from the head groundsman that extreme heat and a Bollywood film shoot hampered preparations.

The sanction drops the county to the bottom of the Division One standings, though the club has until 29 September to appeal.

While Leicestershire defeated Glamorgan on 20 August, the match referee noted 43 instances of unpredictable bounce caused by cracks in the surface. Regulators subsequently declared the Grace Road pitch below required standards, stripping the 19 points gained from the victory and adding an eight-point penalty.

A further eight-point deduction remains suspended until the end of the season in the event of any subsequent pitch breaches.

Leicestershire's head groundsman Callum Lewin argued that extenuating circumstances prevented him from maintaining the playing area effectively.

"There was a lot of circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control, such as the weather was 35 degrees (Celsius, 95 Fahrenheit) and we had an unscheduled Bollywood filming event four days before," Lewin told the England and Wales Cricket Board's regulator. "I wasn't allowed to work on the pitch. I wasn't allowed to cover it or anything."

Lewin noted that moisture levels consequently dropped below targets, despite heavy watering following eight uninterrupted hours under a scorching sun.

However, the regulatory authority rejected the defense, pointing out that filming occupied just one day and that responsibility for protective measures ultimately lay with the club.

"Risk management should have envisaged the need to incorporate protection of the pitch during the Bollywood event," the regulator stated.

The judgment was delivered late on Wednesday night while Leicestershire were playing Hampshire in their penultimate match of the campaign.

That leaves one remaining game on their schedule, a visit to Warwickshire starting on 24 September.

The filming at the ground was reportedly for an upcoming biopic about former India captain Sourav Ganguly.

A stylish stroke maker, Ganguly scored 16 test and 22 one-day international centuries, accumulating over 18,000 runs across both formats, and played county championship cricket in the early 2000s.

articles.title: Arsenal confirm signing of Liverpool youth striker
articles.summary: Arsenal have confirmed the transfer of Liverpool youth striker Vincent Joseph, with the player signing a scholarship agreement to play in north London.Photo...
articles.body:
Arsenal have confirmed the transfer of Liverpool youth striker Vincent Joseph, with the player signing a scholarship agreement to play in north London.

Arsenal have officially announced the signing of Vincent Joseph , following the young striker's decision to run down his contract with former club Liverpool .

The club report that Joseph is joining as part of Arsenal's first-year scholarship intake for the 2026/27 season, with the player expected to continue his development in u18 football after his debut at that level last season.

Liverpool had made an effort to convince Joseph to stay, offering him a scholarship contract this summer, but he turned them down.

Despite Joseph being out of contract with Liverpool, a compensation fee still needed to be agreed due to his age.

Reports in August suggested that the two clubs had failed to reach a deal agreement, and the matter would go to a tribunal. That tribunal evidently reached a positive resolution.

As mentioned, Joseph made his breakthrough into u18 Premier League football last season, scoring three goals in his two appearances for Liverpool.

The young striker has also scored eight goals in his nine games for the England u16s, with all of those appearances coming in the course of the 2025/26 campaign.

Arsenal have been on the lookout for youth strikers in recent transfer windows, and they missed out on Will Wright to Liverpool just last year.

But after completing moves for Blackburn Rovers' Igor Tyjon , Crystal Palace 's Mylo Bernard and now Liverpool's Joseph, the Gunners seem to have found their attacking academy additions.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Could Get Massive Defensive Reinforcements After Bills Game
articles.summary: Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph become eligible to open 21-day practice windows after Week 2, though neither can play until Week 5.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions still have to get through Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.

After that, attention could quickly turn toward two of the most important players missing from Detroit's defense.

Safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are currently on Reserve/PUP, which requires them to miss the first four games of the season. Under the NFL's updated rules, however, players on Reserve/PUP can begin a 21-day practice window after their team's second game , meaning Detroit becomes eligible to start that process once Thursday night is complete.

Dr. Jimmy Liao, who tracks Lions injuries extensively, noted Thursday morning that Branch has a decent chance of having his practice window opened, while Joseph's timeline remains much less certain. His 2026 Lions injury tracker currently projects Branch's return in the October-November range and lists Joseph's return timetable as uncertain.

Opening the Window Does Not Mean Branch Can Play

Detroit placed both starting safeties on Reserve/PUP when it established its initial roster, officially guaranteeing that Branch and Joseph would miss at least the first four regular-season games. The Lions announced both moves on Aug. 30 .

So even if Branch returns to the practice field next week, he cannot appear in a game until Week 5 at the earliest .

Opening the practice window is not the same as activating a player. It simply allows Detroit to begin integrating that player into practice while evaluating whether he is physically ready for game action.

Branch has been recovering from the torn Achilles he suffered last December. Campbell said during training camp that Branch's rehabilitation remained on schedule, and Detroit hoped he could return to practice sometime around the beginning of the regular season.

That makes the possibility of a practice return after Week 2 noteworthy.

It would be the clearest sign yet that Branch is approaching the final stage of his recovery.

Joseph's situation has always carried more uncertainty.

The All-Pro safety has dealt with a lingering knee problem dating back to last season, one that eventually forced him to miss the final 11 games of 2025.

Campbell acknowledged throughout the offseason that Detroit simply would not know how Joseph's knee responded until the rehabilitation process advanced.

When camp opened, Campbell said Joseph was running and beginning change-of-direction work but cautioned that the Lions still had "a long way to go." The team ultimately decided to put him on Reserve/PUP alongside Branch.

The more recent update has not dramatically changed that picture.

Detroit's own Tim Twentyman wrote last week that Joseph was back in the building and ramping up his rehab but that there was still no clear answer regarding when his knee would be ready for football.

Detroit Has Been Surviving Without Its Star Safety Duo

They entered the season with veteran Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox handling the starting safety roles while Branch and Joseph remained unavailable.

Detroit specifically added experienced depth because of those injuries. Clark entered Week 1 with 80 career starts, while Maddox has extensive experience throughout the secondary. The Lions highlighted that experience before the opener .

It has not made Branch and Joseph replaceable.

Branch has become one of the NFL's most versatile defensive backs, capable of playing safety, nickel, near the line of scrimmage and as a pressure player. Joseph has developed into one of football's premier ball-hawking safeties, recording 20 interceptions since entering the league in 2022.

We broke down Detroit's decision to place both players on PUP when Campbell provided his late-August update on Branch and Joseph .

Their return would change the ceiling of this defense.

Branch Practicing Would Be a Significant First Step

Detroit has not officially announced that either practice window will open, and even if Branch is cleared to practice, there will still be a process before he is ready for live game action.

But after months of rehabilitation, the calendar is finally reaching the point where something tangible can happen.

The Lions have spent the first month of the season knowing Branch and Joseph cannot help them on Sundays.

After Thursday night, that changes slightly.

Neither can play before Week 5, but simply getting Branch back onto the field at Allen Park would represent meaningful progress for a Detroit defense waiting to get two of its best players back.

For the first time this season, the countdown could be moving from months to weeks .

articles.title: Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers fires back at reporter questioning Roman Wilson’s targets
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers dismissed concerns over Roman Wilson's targets.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers opened the 2026 NFL season with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons . Star quarterback Aaron Rodgers completed 24 of 40 passes for 221 yards and one touchdown. But it was one moment after the game involving a question about Roman Wilson 's target count that drew attention.

Wilson received six targets, tied for second on Pittsburgh behind DK Metcalf 's 10. He finished with three receptions for 26 yards, starting his second season with the Steelers.

When a reporter highlighted Wilson's target total, Rodgers quickly pushed back on the premise.

"I don't give a s–t about the target list," Rodgers said.

He then explained why he does not focus on individual target numbers.

"The ball goes to the open guy," Rodgers said. "… Nobody in the locker room talks about their targets. That's all for you guys to talk about."

Rodgers also made it clear that Wilson has earned his confidence. The quarterback praised the young receiver for his performance against Atlanta and his work during training camp.

"I love Roman. I think he's done a great job," Rodgers said. "… I thought he played fast last week, played decisive, and I think he's just gonna keep on getting better."

Aaron Rodgers' approach fits Steelers' offensive structure

Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) talks at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Rodgers' comments reflect how the veteran quarterback wants to keep individual production from disrupting offensive roles. The Steelers have several receiving options, which makes defensive reads and situational execution more important than predetermined target totals.

Pittsburgh had possession of the ball for only 28:53 minutes against Atlanta and had only 264 yards in the game. So, there is clearly a need for improvement despite getting the win, especially for a team with playoff aspirations.

The defense carried much of the workload. T.J. Watt recorded two sacks and returned a Cooper Rush interception 35 yards for a touchdown, while Pittsburgh finished with four sacks.

Wilson's role should therefore be judged over multiple games rather than one target total. Rodgers has already indicated that the ball will go where the offense finds opportunities.

That approach keeps Pittsburgh's focus on execution instead of individual statistics. The Steelers will next face the New England Patriots on Sunday, providing another test for Rodgers and the team's offense.
