articles.title: ”Las declaraciones de Mbappé son un lavado de imagen pensando en el Balón de Oro”
articles.standfirst: 'El Corrillo' es el espacio de opinión de Directo MARCA
articles.summary: 'El Corrillo' es el espacio de opinión de Directo MARCA
articles.body: Manu Martín, Joan Prats, Javier Tintó y Alberto Pérez han sido los tertulianos de 'El Corrillo' en 'Directo MARCA' con Rafa Sahuquillo en Radio MARCA, en un debate que ha protagonizado el último partido del Real Madrid contra el Elche. El derbi madrileño dividió a los tertulianos de El Corrillo, aunque tres de los cuatro ven al Atlético ligeramente por delante en este momento. Manu Martín, que pronosticó un 3-1, aseguró que ve "a un Atlético de Madrid más rodado en este arranque" y añadió que, entre dos equipos que van "de menos a más", "el que saca una rueda en la línea de meta es el Atleti". Joan Prats, que apostó por un 3-2, coincidió: "El Atlético llega un poquito mejor en dinámica y confianza, y el Madrid sigue teniendo esa falta de fiabilidad". Alberto Pérez, con un 2-1, también se inclinó por los rojiblancos: "Aquí lo veo muy igualado y lo desnivelo un poquito por esa fuerza del Metropolitano, donde hay muy pocos equipos en Europa que puedan ganar". El único que se decantó por el conjunto blanco fue Javi Tintó, con un 1-2: "Creo que el Madrid va a ganar el partido porque va a tener un poquito más de pegada que el Atleti". El momento del Real Madrid abrió otro de los grandes debates de la tertulia, especialmente por su falta de contundencia y los bajones durante los partidos. Javi Tintó defendió que el problema no está en generar ocasiones: "Lo que le está fallando a este Madrid es la pegada. El Madrid ha cambiado radicalmente, no hemos visto un Madrid que llegara tanto al área y a la portería en años". Joan Prats, en cambio, puso el foco en la falta de control: "Me está dejando muchas dudas. Deja fases del partido en las que pierde el control, el equipo se parte, concede muchos metros también a la espalda del centro del campo". Manu Martín pidió tiempo para el proyecto y sostuvo que "este Real Madrid va a ir a más", aunque reconoció que "tiene mucho margen de mejora". Alberto Pérez incidió en el potencial de la plantilla: "Creo que el Atleti, colectivamente, me parece un equipo mejor estructurado, pero el Madrid individualmente es mejor". La polémica por las camisetas de apoyo a Ceuta ocupó buena parte de El Corrillo, con especial atención a la actuación de los jugadores y a la gestión del Real Madrid. Joan Prats consideró que los futbolistas "deciden saltarse la norma institucional y anteponer su decisión personal o su opinión personal a la institucional", algo que, a su juicio, "es un error". Javi Tintó defendió la libertad de los jugadores para no sumarse al gesto, aunque criticó la imagen ofrecida: "Nadie tiene que estar obligado a apoyar ninguna causa", pero "el error para mí de los tres jugadores" fue ponerse la camiseta a medias. Manu Martín apuntó directamente a la gestión de la escena: "La única culpa que puede tener el Madrid es de no haber atajado la situación en el túnel de vestuarios", mientras que sobre las explicaciones posteriores de Mbappé fue tajante: "Lo que has hecho ha sido enfollonar, enmerdar y enfangar más la cosa". Alberto Pérez, por su parte, calificó de "surrealista" lo sucedido y señaló que "la camiseta puesta como un top ya me parece que es un desprecio en general a la situación", al tiempo que valoró el viaje institucional: "Creo que el Real Madrid debe hacerlo y está muy bien hecho".

articles.title: Chesnes developing as a leader for Falcons girls soccer team
articles.summary: JEFFERSON — What do you get when you have a freshman with sprinter’s speed, high soccer IQ and the experience of playing on a club team? For the Jefferson Fa...
articles.body:
JEFFERSON — What do you get when you have a freshman with sprinter's speed, high soccer IQ and the experience of playing on a club team?

For the Jefferson Falcons, the answer is Charleigh Chesnes, and she is just the type of player the Falcons girls soccer team needed to build their team around.

The freshman scored four goals Tuesday night as the Falcons defeated Lakeside 7-0 in a Chagrin Valley Lake Division match to snap a four-game losing streak at Falcon Pride Stadium.

Chesnes said she had scored three times in a game before, but not four.

She has 10 goals on the season now, and is a big reason Jefferson has hopes of a winning season.

Aside from her high school team, Chesnes plays for SPIRE Academy.

High School soccer in the area is not quite the same as club, but Chesnes said that doesn't bother her the least.

"I still enjoy it," she said with a smile. "It's not as competitive as SPIRE, but I still have fun with the girls."

The Falcons are having fun, but many of them are learning as they go, and because they're winning a little more often this season.

After winning their first two matches of the season, Jefferson lost four straight, before getting back into the win column Tuesday night in improving to 3-4 overall, 1-3 in the conference.

The Falcons have multiple players either on a club team or travel soccer.

It puts Chesnes in a spot where, like it or not, she's called on to be a leader.

Sharing what she knows about the game, though, is something she's enjoying.

"I watched a lot of the World Cup this summer," she said. "I think it's just from how many years I've played to how much I've seen of soccer compared to the other girls. I definitely help out on the field and tell them where they need to be, that sort of thing."

Jefferson coach Brian Kereky said Chesnes is learning to be more vocal, and knows where to be and what she needs to be doing at all times.

"Charleigh is very quiet," he said. "Personally, I rely on her because I've coached her for a long time and I know what she can do. She does a wonderful job and she's been the most consistent player I've had."

Having Chesnes is a big help, but the coach said that there's been some other positives this fall, namely having more players out than any year in recent memory.

What the team wants most, though is a winning season, something Jefferson has not had in quite a while, maybe ever. A year ago, the Falcons won just one game, but Chesnes said the team believes they can make a dramatic improvement this season.

"I think we can have a winning record from here on out if we play the way we're capable of," she said. "So long as we play together and don't have any injuries or anything like that."

Kereky believes the team can as well, but the coach also is looking at the bigger picture.

"I don't think we've ever had one," he said of a winning season. "I think we won six games in one year. Hopefully, we can do it, but winning is not everything. It's about bringing the girls back and getting new girls out, keep building the program."

Jefferson will be back at home for Conneaut tonight, before heading to Pymatuning Valley Saturday.

Lakeside, which fell to 2-6 overall, 0-5, is scheduled to play Tuesday at Conneaut.
authors: Mike Shaffer, Star Beacon, Ashtabula, Ohio

articles.title: Conneaut excited to play perennial state power Kirtland
articles.summary: KIRTLAND — Undefeated through their first four games of the 2026 football campaign, the Conneaut Spartans are off to their best start since Rocco Dobran took...
articles.body:
KIRTLAND — Undefeated through their first four games of the 2026 football campaign, the Conneaut Spartans are off to their best start since Rocco Dobran took over the program 16 years ago.

It's also the best start in school history since the early 1980s.

Led by a strong senior class and, according to Dobran, depth like he hasn't had before, the Spartans have used that to record some impressive wins to open the season.

Cuyahoga Heights, Jefferson, Edgewood and Berkshire — Conneaut's first four opponents — all were quality wins for the Spartans.

On Friday, however, Conneaut will be presented with a challenge it has not encountered yet.

The Spartans will go to to Kirtland High School in a Chagrin Valley Conference Valley Division game.

When Conneaut and Kirtland kick it off at 7 p.m. Friday at Wilson Stadium, Dobran's crew not only will be facing the best team it has played this season — it will go against one of the best in Ohio.

"The end goal for everyone is a state championship, so this is a chance for us to see 'where do we stack up?'" Dobran said. "We are excited to see where we fall."

Dobran said much of Conneaut's early success this season is due to the leadership displayed by his senior class.

"We're more athletic than we've been in a long time," he said. "And, this team is a little more player-led than coach-led, which is a good thing."

That leadership has been on display all season, according to Dobran, and especially in practice this week.

"They are excited," he said. "The kids are taking practice seriously, but they are also having a good time with it. We are going to give it everything we've got. We are not going to worry about the scoreboard, and at the end, we will see what it says."

Dobran said his players believe that "anything can happen in any game," and the Spartans are approaching this week with that mindset.

The coach also knows that seeing the best — regardless of that scoreboard — will pay dividends for his program.

"Even if things don't go our way, it allows our kids to say, 'what do we have to do to get to where they are and what is it that they do that gets them to that spot every year?," Dobran said.

Kirtland returns its entire starting line from a year ago, but has had an overhaul among its skilled positions, having graduated the entire group from its 15-0 team which won the Ohio High School Athletic Association Division VI state title last season.

This season, however, the Hornets — except in the second half against Perry in which it was held scoreless — have not missed a beat. Kirtland is averaging nearly 37 points a game, and has punted just twice through the first four weeks.

"I guess that's a good sign," Hornets coach Tiger LaVerde said of how quickly his new crew has put it together in attaining a 3-1 overall, 1-0 conference record.

Junior Ben Loncar has been efficient in his first year as a varsity quarterback for the Hornets.

He, along with senior running backs Zander Perkins, Sebastian Becker, and Tommy Caimi, were all standouts on defense last year. This season, they've taken on pivotal roles on offense, running behind an experienced line led by four-year starting center Luci Cantini.

From watching Kirtland on film, Dobran summed up the formula for Kirtland's success.

"They coach fundamentals and effort," he said. "Their players are in great shape and they go hard to the whistle on every play. And, they really simplify what they do. They aren't fancy. Many times you know what they are going to do, but they just do it really well."

LaVerde said Conneaut also does a lot well, and is impressed with the size and athleticism he saw from the Spartans on film.

"I think they have good size at the skill positions," LaVerde said. "Rocco's son [Wyant] is the quarterback. He is smart and makes really good decisions. They put him in a lot of RPO's [run-pass options] and he makes good reads and puts them in good situations."

Senior Wyant Dobran has amassed 531 yards passing and five touchdowns, to go with another 187 yards rushing and four more scores on the ground.

Three Spartans — 6'3" senior Davonte Harris, 5'10" senior Aiden Goudge, and 6'1" junior Jacob Thompson — each have more than 100 yards receiving on the year.

And, 5'11" senior running back Isaiah Boles continues to be a focal point of defenses, catching the eye of opposing coaches with his athleticism and hard running style.

"Their running back has good size, good wheels and runs downhill hard," LaVerde said of Boles. "It will be a great challenge for us."

Friday's game also marks Kirtland's first home contest this season.

"It should be a fun game," LaVerde said. "We haven't played them [Conneaut] since I have been here. It should be a fun night for us regardless because it is our first home game. The town's going to be excited to host a game, finally."

For even those familiar with the task at hand, it's worth noting Kirtland's dominance under the leadership of LaVerde since he took over the program in the 2006 season.

He has compiled a 262-22 overall record in his tenure at the school, becoming the fastest coach in OHSAA history to reach 200 and 250 wins, respectively.

The record includes eight OHSAA championships.

In his 21st season leading the Hornets program, LaVerde has lost just nine regular-season games.

The Hornets have lost more than one regular season game only one time, and that dates back to the 2009 campaign, in LaVerde's tenure at Kirtland.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving offers to pay Azeez Al-Shaair's fine
articles.summary: The NFL has fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for having a personal message written on his black eye strips during the Week 1 game against the...
articles.body:
The NFL has fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for having a personal message written on his black eye strips during the Week 1 game against the Bills. Mavericks star Kyrie Irving has Al-Shaair covered.

" I'll take care of his fine ," Irving said on social media, via ESPN.

Al-Shaair, who was fined in January for wearing "stop the genocide" on his eye-black strips, played Sunday's game with the name "Hind Rajab" written in the space. The five-year-old girl was killed by Israeli forces, along with six members of her family, when their car came under fire in Gaza City in 2024.

The league generally prohibits any personal messaging without prior approval.

The league also prohibits the payment of fines by anyone other than the person being fined. But that can't stop Irving from giving Al-Shaair a gift in the amount of, say, $11,941, if Irving so chooses.

And while Al-Shaair is doing well enough to pay the fine on his own, with a contract that pays out on average $18 million per year, Irving is making nearly $40 million in 2026-27.

The next question is whether Al-Shaair will try to do it again in Week 2 against the Bengals, and whether he'll be prevented from playing. After he was fined for having the message on his eye black during the wild-card win at Pittsburgh, Al-Shaair was told he'd not be permitted to play in the divisional round at New England if he tried to do it again.

articles.title: Klopp wants to 'reclaim' flag amid German elections
articles.summary: New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.
articles.body:
New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.

The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won 43.8% of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, falling just short of securing an absolute majority in the regional parliament.

The anti-immigration party also expects strong results in elections on Sunday in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

Speaking at a news conference to announce his first squad, Klopp stressed he is not a political "expert" but added: "We had an election where some people may have thought it was OK, while others were saying, 'my God, what is happening here?'

"From my perspective as a sportsman, I can say that I would very much like to reclaim the flag for myself, for all of us.

"I want it so that when someone waves it, no one thinks: 'What is wrong with you?' Instead, I want people to understand: You are happy and realise how lucky you were to be born, grow up, or move to this wonderful country."

No far-right party has controlled a German state since World War Two, when the ruling Nazi party carried out the Holocaust.

"I do not want to entrust national pride to the wrong people," said Klopp, who prefers the term "positive patriotism" to "national pride", which he fears can be misunderstood.

The former Liverpool boss added: "I can be proud to be German while also being open-minded and diverse, and kind and friendly."

Klopp also said it was more important that the country had enough doctors and caregivers but said football can "foster a sense of community, so that people can truly feel the power of sport".

Klopp named 16 uncapped players in a 44-man squad for four upcoming Nations League matches over the space of two weeks.

A group of 24 players will be available against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on 24 September and at home to Greece in Augsburg three days later.

Most of those players will then return to their clubs while the other 20 players will join the group before Germany face Serbia in Munich on 1 October and Greece in Thessaloniki on 4 October.

The first group includes Premier League trio Kai Havertz ( Arsenal ), Kevin Schade ( Brentford ) and Anton Stach ( Leeds ), while Jamal Musiala is selected after twice collapsing during pre-season games for Bayern Munich .

Brentford's Vitaly Janelt has received his first call-up as part of the second group, which also includes Florian Wirtz (Liverpool) and Malick Thiaw (Newcastle).

Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and defender Antonio Rudiger retired from international duty after Germany's second-round exit against Paraguay at this summer's World Cup.

That led to the departure of coach Julian Nagelsmann and the subsequent appointment of Klopp, who had been working as global head of soccer for Red Bull.

articles.body:
Despite being 39 and playing in the MLS, Lionel Messi is still among the 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees.

The Inter Miami star played a key role in his team winning the MLS Cup for the first time in 2025.

More recently, he was among the World Cup's top goalscorers as Argentina reached the second final in a row before losing 1-0 to Spain.

Now, 433 have shared that Messi had more goal involvements than any other Ballon d'Or nominee across 2025/26.

Lionel Messi had the most goal involvements across 2025/26

They tweeted: "Lionel Messi (85 G+A) leads the way in total goal involvements during the 2025-26 season, while Harry Kane (81) scored the most goals."

The South American managed 53 goals and 32 assists during that period.

Harry Kane took second place on the list (73 goals, 8 assists). Real Madrid and France star Kylian Mbappe was third (58 goals, 13 assists).

Norwegian striker Erling Haaland placed fourth (58 goals, 12 assists), while Michael Olise (25 goals, 37 assists) rounded out the top five.

Messi (8) has already won more Ballon d'Ors than any other player in history prior to the 2026 ceremony, with Cristiano Ronaldo (5) his closest competitor.

articles.title: 3 Reasons Georgia Tech Bowl Hopes Just Crumbled After Loss
articles.summary: Georgia Tech's bowl chances are fading fast. A 14-13 loss to Colorado has experts dropping the Yellow Jackets from postseason projections.
articles.body:
Georgia Tech is now on the outside looking in for a bowl game after a heartbreaking loss to Colorado . The Yellow Jackets started the season 0-2 after losses to Colorado and Tennessee . Sports Illustrated reported that the preseason win total of 6.5 has already sunk to 5.5. If the team wants to make its fourth straight postseason appearance, they must play better immediately or face a historic miss. CBS Sports dropped the Jackets from their projections entirely, while ESPN's Kyle Bonagura did the same. Only one national analyst, Mark Schlabach, still has them in the picture, sending them to the Gasparilla Bowl to face Tulane. That is a tall order for a team that just lost in Atlanta.

The loss to the Buffaloes was ugly in the trenches. Colorado rushed for 183 yards while holding Georgia Tech to just 51. The Yellow Jackets averaged only 1.7 yards per carry, which allowed the visitors to control the line of scrimmage. With 42 seconds remaining, Julian Lewis orchestrated the decisive drive and linked up with Charlie Williams for the go-ahead score. Boo Carter blocked the field goal as time expired, thwarting Georgia Tech's attempt to win. After the Colorado loss, Georgia Tech was projected as an underdog against Tennessee, Virginia Tech , Pittsburgh, Louisville , Clemson and Georgia. .

Coming into the year, the Jackets were favored in six games and underdogs in six. That balance is gone. They are now double-digit underdogs this Saturday against Tennessee. Virginia Tech, Pittsburgh, Louisville, Clemson, and Georgia will also present underdog matchups for them.Mercer is up next for Georgia Tech on Sept. 19, while Boston College comes later on Oct. 24. The team needs to stop the bleeding now. The loss to Colorado exposed a lack of size that the Buffaloes exploited all afternoon. Deion Sanders' squad entered as a 6.5-point underdog but left with a victory that stunned the local crowd.

The defense did get some individual recognition despite the loss. Lamont Lester Jr earned the Walter Camp National Defensive Player of the Week honor. He recorded five tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, and three sacks in the game. No Colorado player since 2003 recorded more sacks in a debut game than those three. It is the fourth time since 2004 that a Colorado player has earned this specific honor. Chauncey Gooden earned Outland Trophy National Player of the Week recognition for his dual-line performance. He started at guard but played defensive tackle late in the game. The Football Writers Association of America bestowed this award due to his two-way contributions. Per reports, Gooden excelled in the running game on an offensive line rated 91.5 in pass protection and 84.5 in run blocking.

The rankings took a hit, but the real damage is in the win column. Four points went to Georgia Tech in the preseason Associated Press Top 25 poll. After traveling to Atlanta and defeating the Yellow Jackets, Colorado received only three points in the subsequent rankings. The US LBM Coaches Poll offered even less enthusiasm, awarding the Buffaloes a single vote. Finishing 3–9 the prior season left Coach Prime's squad with no votes initially, yet they escaped Atlanta victorious. Questions regarding size, physicality, and recovery from the previous year surrounded the Buffaloes, who were predicted to finish near the Big 12 bottom. They answered those questions with a dominant ground game.

To secure their fourth straight bowl appearance under Brent Key, Georgia Tech must start performing much better. ESPN's Mark Schlabach, the sole national analyst keeping the Yellow Jackets in postseason contention, projected them to the Gasparilla Bowl against Tulane. Having defeated UCF in the 2023 Gasparilla Bowl, the Yellow Jackets are familiar with their opponent. But the path to get there is now a mountain climb. Six games favored them and six favored opponents as they entered the year. Now, the odds are stacked against them. The team must fix the run defense or the season will end before it truly begins.

Chelsea fans are desperate to find out the status of Moises Caicedo – but their manager isn't giving much away at all.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Moises Caicedo has played just a handful of minutes for Chelsea this season, and fans are obsessed over his return.

Not only is he a top player, he's also the exact central midfield force it feels like this team is missing. There's a growing (perhaps overoptimistic) view that his return instantly levels this team up.

But we still don't know when we will see him, and Xabi Alonso's press conferences aren't revealing anything more than the bare minimum.

"He's getting closer and tomorrow we will make the final decision," in his usual vague manner.

Caicedo could benefit massively from one more missed game

Moises Caicedo (Photo by Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

As we wrote earlier in the week, we think Caicedo will sit this one out on the basis that he can then justifiably miss the entire three week international break with Ecuador , allowing a nice long break to get up to speed.

It might mean sacrificing points tomorrow night, but it's a risk worth taking if it really means he gets that time off. Having him come into mid-October with effectively zero minutes in his legs could give him a brilliant platform for the rest of the season.

Alonso was equally non-specific about the availability of Joao Pedro , who has pulled out of the Brazil squad.

articles.title: Commanders WR Stefon Diggs addressed teammates after costly penalty vs Eagles
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs addressed his teammates after his penalty on Sunday vs. Eagles.
articles.body:
When leaders disappoint their group, how should they respond?

On Monday, Commanders WR Stefon Diggs addressed the team and said he was wrong to draw an unsportsmanlike penalty. Diggs drew the penalty immediately after catching a touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels. The touchdown brought the Commanders to within two points (17-15) of the Eagles . However, his 15-yard penalty cost the Commanders dearly, meaning they could not try for two points to tie the game. They had to settle instead for a 48-yard extra-point attempt, which Drew Stevens converted, making the score 17-16 Philadelphia.

The penalty was a missed opportunity to tie the game, and the blame fell squarely on Diggs. So he spoke to the team. WUSA9 sports anchor Marshall Kramsky asked Diggs about it Wednesday.

"My biggest thing was I am accountable," conveyed Diggs. "I always admit I am human. But I'm accountable way more than I am human. This is a team sport, and I feel like as a leader on this team I always want to win."

"If you really want to win, you want to do everything to put the team in a position to win...things happen; you try to move forward. I told them I was accountable; that was number one. I just wanted to say it to the team. I don't wanna brush anything under the rug. I don't want things to go unnoticed."

Good for Diggs. He is correct; he cost the team the opportunity to tie the game at 17-17. It doesn't mean they would have, but it does mean they had to go for two late in the game instead of simply kicking to tie the game at 24-24. He is correct in confessing to the team because he let them down. He further didn't make excuses for his poor choice; he owned it.

By doing this, Diggs might be helping set a culture of not making excuses when players make poor choices. As a result, he stands a better chance of earning the respect of teammates who themselves understand the importance of being responsible for the choices you make and owning them.

articles.title: 'We need the fans more than ever' - Henderson's plea
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Dean Henderson says Crystal Palace fans deserve the current period of success "more than anyone", but believes there is a need to "park the negati...
articles.body:
Goalkeeper Dean Henderson says Crystal Palace fans deserve the current period of success "more than anyone", but believes there is a need to "park the negativity".

The 29-year-old, who has signed a new, long-term contract until 2030, has made 119 appearances for the Eagles since arriving from Manchester United in August 2023.

Henderson has also lifted the FA Cup and worn the captain's armband in the Conference League during his time at Selhurst Park.

"When we talk about that day out at Wembley Stadium for the FA Cup, obviously the lads were outstanding to a man but the supporters were incredible as well," he told club media .

"I don't think you will ever hear Wembley Stadium that loud again. They were right in our corner every step of the way, kicking every ball when the lads were tired.

"They deserve this period of success more than anyone.

"Selhurst Park is a big thing for us. It needs to become a fortress going forward.

"We need the fans more than ever in this transition period. Obviously, it has been a little bit of a difficult period with the lads getting back late and new ideas coming in.

"I'm so certain that we are going to have a really good season, so we need to park the negativity and all be as one. Together, we will be stronger."
